{{Quote|Even advanced species like the Chiss had found a way to make icy planets into homes.|An artist, in his journal|<ref name="Alien Archive" />}}
'''Csilla''' {{Pronounced|ˈt͡ʃiːlə}} was a [[Temperature|frigid]], [[Water|ice]]-locked [[planet]] in the [[Unknown Regions]]. It was the [[homeworld]] of the [[Sentience|sentient]], [[near-human]] [[Chiss]] [[species]] and the [[capital]] world of the [[Chiss Ascendancy]]. Though largely unknown to the wider [[The galaxy|galaxy]] during the [[Imperial Era|age]] of the Galactic Empire, [[Scout|exploratory]] missions to the Unknown Regions conducted [[Standard year|years]] later revealed Csilla and other worlds that could be reached through cautious [[hyperspace]] jumps.

==Description==
Csilla was a [[Temperature|cold]], [[Water|ice]]-locked [[planet]]<ref name="DoR" /> located in the [[Csilla system]]<ref name="Chaos Rising" /> of the [[Unknown Regions]], at the coordinates F-8<ref name="TFABG" /> on the [[Standard Galactic Grid]].<ref name="Rebel Dossier">''[[Star Wars: Rogue One: Rebel Dossier]]''</ref> Its capital was the [[city]] of [[Csaplar]], which was mostly located underground.<ref name="Chaos Rising" />

Visitors to Csilla, whether Chiss or [[alien]], were led to believe that the planet remained vibrantly populated despite its shift to much colder weather. The parts of Csilla near the [[Csaplar spaceport]] were bustling, with hotels, entertainment venues, merchants, diplomats, government and military business nearby. However, most of the above-ground parts of Csaplar and other cities were devoid of inhabitants and made to simply look lively to create the appearance of a well-populated world.<ref name="Chaos Rising" />

At the twilight of the [[Clone Wars]], approximately 60–70 million Chiss still lived on Csilla. The vast majority of them lived in illuminated and heated underground caves which could even have forests, lakes, mountains, and convincing artificial sunlight within them. To create the façade of 8 billion inhabitants on Csilla, some of those who lived underground were selected on a rotating basis to spend a limited amount of time on the surface, to appear as if they lived there.<ref name="Chaos Rising" />

==History==
===A great war===
{{Quote|But then, centuries later, came an invasion by a merciless enemy. Our outer worlds were overrun and the Defense Force pushed back until only Csilla remained unconquered. The enemy gathered all its ships and armies, preparing for what is now known as the Final Assault on Csilla. We knew there was no way we could stand against them, and we knew that if we lost the Chiss faced extinction.|translated=1|Lamiov, to Thrass and Thrawn|<ref name="Lesser Evil" />}}
Csilla was inhabited by the [[Chiss]] for thousands of [[Standard year|years]]. Approximately 1000 years before the [[Clone Wars]],<ref name="Chaos Rising" /> during the [[Final Assault on Csilla|climax]] of a great [[Unidentified war (Chiss Ascendancy)|war]] fought between the Chiss Ascendancy and an [[Unidentified enemy of the Chiss|enemy]], the Chiss were forced back to Csilla. Despite their earlier losses, the Chiss Ascendancy were forced to use an ancient alien weapon known as the [[Starflash]]. The sacrifice of all four sons of the [[Mitth family|Mitth]] [[Patriarch]] [[Mitth'omo'rossodo|Thomoro]] destroyed the entire enemy force, saving the Ascendancy from being conquered and securing the Mitth a rank among the [[Ruling Families|Nine Ruling Families]]. However, the weapon also affected [[Csilla's sun]], causing it to cool and make the surface of the planet uninhabitable.<ref name="Lesser Evil" />

===Climate change===
Because of the change in [[temperature]], a vast majority of the planet's four billion residents moved offworld to the planets [[Rentor]], [[Avidich]] and [[Sarvchi]]. Those who remained moved underground. At the time of the Clone Wars, the official records stated that Csilla had a population of eight billion, but the actual population at this time was around sixty to seventy million. To maintain the illusion of a still-thriving planet, several hundred Chiss citizens were stationed near [[Csaplar]]'s spaceports and [[tube car]]s were continually run across the empty city.<ref name="Chaos Rising" />

Csilla was openly attacked in 19 BBY<ref name="CR date">The [[Del Rey]] ''[[Star Wars]]'' timeline places ''Thrawn Ascendancy: Chaos Rising'' after ''[[Dark Disciple]]'' and before [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']]. Furthermore, {{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-clone-wars-chronological-episodeorder|text=''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' Chronological Episode Order}} places ''Dark Disciple'' between "[[A Death on Utapau]]" and ''Revenge of the Sith'', which are dated to [[19 BBY]] by ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]''. Since the events of ''Chaos Rising'' are set between the events of ''Dark Disciple'' and ''Revenge of the Sith'', they must also occur in that [[Standard year|year]].</ref>. Three unknown enemy capital ships emerged from [[hyperspace]] and attacked the orbital defense platforms. The defenders, although shocked momentarily, began firing within a minute and soon destroyed all three of the ships and all wreckage so as to not damage the planet. All leadership on the planet went to underground bunkers and stayed there for several hours to see if there were any follow-up attacks.<ref name="Chaos Rising" />

===Imperial Era===
[[File:ThrawnTreasonCoverArt.png|thumb|left|200px|Joining the ranks of the Empire in the name of supporting the Chiss, Thrawn attempted to withhold the location of his people's territories from the Galactic Emperor, something he noticed.]]
The Chiss and their home planet were largely unknown in other regions of [[the galaxy]]. Consequently, when an [[Galactic Empire|Imperial]] scouting party led by [[Captain]] [[Voss Parck]] encountered the supposedly [[Exile (punishment)|exiled]] Chiss [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo|Thrawn]]<ref name="Thrawn">[[Thrawn (novel)|''Thrawn'']]</ref> in circa [[15 BBY]],<ref name="Thrawn Beginning date">{{ThrawnNovelStartDate}}</ref> Parck instructed [[Imperial cadet|cadet]] [[Eli N. Vanto|Eli Vanto]] to learn anything he could from the [[alien]] about his species and homeworld.<ref name="Thrawn" /> In secret, Thrawn's motives were to see if the Empire would be a suitable ally for the [[Chiss–Grysk conflict]] or if it could be weakened from within to be a more suitable target. Upon meeting [[Galactic Emperor]] [[Darth Sidious|Sheev Palpatine]], however, Thrawn would find himself with a new opportunity and entered the ranks of the [[Imperial Navy]].<ref name="Thrawn: Treason">''[[Thrawn: Treason]]''</ref>

As continued his career in the Imperial Navy and became an advisor on the mapping of the Unknown Regions for Palpatine, Thrawn—who would arise to the rank of [[Grand Admiral]]<ref name="Thrawn" /> in [[2 BBY]]<ref name="Timelines">''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]''</ref>—would withhold the location of Chiss planets and bases from the Emperor, something Palpatine noticed but claimed did not annoy him.<ref name="Thrawn" /> In truth, however, Palpatine—when confronted by Thrawn about the coming [[Grysk Hegemony]]<ref name="Thrawn: Treason" /> in [[1 BBY]]<ref name="Timelines" />—decided the best defense would be the annex the Chiss territories into his Empire. He intended to force Thrawn to help him in his conquest,<ref name="Thrawn: Treason" /> but the efforts of the Jedi-in-training [[Ezra Bridger]] during the [[Liberation of Lothal|Battle of Lothal]] took Thrawn out of galactic affairs<ref name="Family&Farewell">{{Rebels|Family Reunion – and Farewell}}</ref> for years to come,<ref name="Part 7">{{Ahsoka|Part Seven: Dreams and Madness}}</ref> ruining Palpatine's plans.<ref name="Thrawn: Treason" />

In [[4 ABY]],<ref name="Galactic Atlas">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]''</ref> the [[Force spirit]] of the [[Jedi]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]] told his apprentice [[Luke Skywalker]] the fate of Csilla, and many other planets, would rely on him confronting the [[Sith Lord]] [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]] in the [[Battle of Endor]].<ref name="Odyssey">''[[The Odyssey of Star Wars: An Epic Poem]]''</ref> Sometime after the [[Battle of Crait]]<ref name="GEG">''[[Star Wars: The Galactic Explorer's Guide]]''</ref> in [[34 ABY]],<ref name="TFA and TLJ Date Note">''[[Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: The Visual Dictionary]]'' places the [[Battle of Crait]] in the same [[Standard year|year]] as the [[Battle of Starkiller Base]], which ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'' dates to [[34 ABY]]</ref> the [[pirate]] [[Hondo Ohnaka]] included Csilla in the [[Galaxy|galactic]] map of his book named the ''[[Galactic Explorer's Guide]]''.<ref name="GEG" /> Although dangerous [[Hyperspace anomaly|hyperspace anomalies]] limited [[Scout|exploration]] of the Unknown Regions, the occasional exploratory missions of the region conducted<ref name="RoS VD">''[[Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> by [[35 ABY]]<ref name="35 ABY date">According to ''[[Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: The Visual Dictionary]]'', the events of [[Star Wars: Episode IX The Rise of Skywalker|''Star Wars'': Episode IX ''The Rise of Skywalker'']] take place one [[Standard year|year]] after the [[Hosnian Cataclysm|Starkiller Incident]]. Since ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'' dates the Incident to [[34 ABY]], ''The Rise of Skywalker'' must take place in [[35 ABY]], while all [[Scout|exploratory]] missions into the [[Unknown Regions]] prior to that event likewise happened by 35 [['ABY-BBY' dating system|ABY]].</ref> revealed some navigable worlds—including Csilla, [[Ilum]], and [[Rakata Prime]]—that could be reached through careful hyperspace jumps.<ref name="RoS VD" />

==Inhabitants==
A part of the [[Chiss Ascendancy]],<ref name="Chaos Rising" /> Csilla was the [[homeworld]] of the [[Sentience|sentient]] [[Chiss]] [[species]].<ref name="Alien Archive" />

At some point, an [[Unidentified artist|artist]] traveled around the galaxy and wrote about the Chiss and their ability to settle into icy planets in [[Unidentified artist's journal|his journal]]. The document was later restored and published by the [[Graf Archive]]<ref name="Alien Archive" /> sometime no earlier than 34 ABY<ref name="Year">{{AlienArchiveJournalDate}}</ref> and included a mention of Csilla as the Chiss homeworld.<ref name="Alien Archive" />

==Behind the scenes==
Csilla was first mentioned in the new ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]] on a map featured in the [[2016]] [[StarWars.com]] article [[Where in the Galaxy Are the Worlds of Star Wars: The Force Awakens?|Where in the Galaxy Are the Worlds of ''Star Wars: The Force Awakens''?]].<ref name="TFA Where in the Galaxy">{{SW|url=news/where-in-the-galaxy-are-the-worlds-of-star-wars-the-force-awakens|text=Where in the Galaxy Are the Worlds of ''Star Wars: The Force Awakens''?|int=Where in the Galaxy Are the Worlds of Star Wars: The Force Awakens?}}</ref> Csilla made its first canonical appearance in [[Timothy Zahn]]'s [[2020]] novel, ''[[Thrawn Ascendancy: Chaos Rising]]'', the first installment in ''[[Star Wars: The Ascendancy Trilogy]]''.<ref name="Chaos Rising" />
